maria: ran an nsys on the failing repro (attached link) — timeline shows lots of tiny HtoD memcpy bursts from the prefetch worker that appear to serialize small kernels on the default compute stream. timeline: https://perf.example/trace/1801234567

tonny: do you mean the prefetch thread is doing host->device for each kv entry? that would create a ton of small memcpys.

maria: yes — KV prefetch currently issues cudaMemcpyAsync per-entry and we keep one shared stream for prefetches. nsys slice shows memcpy on stream 3 then kernels on stream 1 waiting ~2.1ms each time.

han: related: I noticed CPU scheduling gaps in the OS lane right before the big memcpy bursts. there's a 70-120ms lull where the prefetch thread was TASK_RUNNING but not scheduled, then it wakes and issues a backlog of memcpys.

maria: exact nsys capture command I used: ```nsys profile --sample=none --trace=cuda,osrt --output=pkv_prefetch --force ./run_repro.sh```

perf-bot: perf-regression alert: tail latency p99 up 2.6x since regression A (linked). Possible root cause: batching heuristic changed to prefetch aggressively for single-token batches.

tony: a few quick hypotheses: 1) per-entry memcpy on same low-priority stream is causing implicit stream serialization; 2) prefetch thread being preempted leads to bursty behavior; 3) kernels are small (<= 500us) so any serialization kills throughput.

han: evidence for (2): `perf top` during capture shows the prefetch thread running on core 7 but gets preempted by other system work (kworker spikes). We should try pinning the prefetch worker to an isolated core and see if the bursts disappear.

maria: I repro'd with two changes: (A) coalesce prefetch into 8-entry batches, (B) set pthread_setaffinity to core 2 for prefetch. coalesce reduced number of memcpy ops by ~7x in the trace and flattened the timeline. p99 dropped back ~30%.

tonny: good. Another mitigation: use cudaMemPrefetchAsync to the device and rely on UVM (if model fits), or allocate a prefetch staging buffer and do a single big memcpy per batch. Also consider cudaStreamAttachMemAsync patterns to avoid priority inversion.

maria: going to prototype 8-entry coalescing + pinning + make prefetch use high-priority stream with cudaStreamCreateWithPriority. will run nsys again and push a perf branch.

han: one more nit: kernel selection logic currently picks small unoptimized kernels for short sequences; if we detect prefetch backlog, maybe force a larger-kernel path (fewer kernel launches) until backlog clears. could be a temporary heuristic to avoid launch overhead.

tonny: agree — a backpressure signal from the prefetch queue to the batcher would let us increase coalescing dynamically. add a simple metric: current_pending_prefetches > 32 triggers aggressive coalescing.

maria: ok PR plan: (1) coalesce prefetch (toggle via runtime flag), (2) pin prefetch worker to isolated core, (3) create prefetch stream with higher priority, (4) add metric & backpressure hook in batcher. I'll tag you both in the PR.

perf-bot: scheduled nsys rerun job: job id pkv-1801234567-retest. expected runtime 15m.

tonny: thanks — if the nsys rerun confirms flattening of memcpys and no CPU scheduling gaps, we can roll this as a patch to dedicated clusters and keep as a feature flag for hosted. :thumbsup:

maria: uploading the initial trace + before/after screenshots to the ticket: https://tickets.example/RED-789

han: ack, will help validate on a 16-gpu dense cluster tomorrow.

maria: quick log snippet from the trace (nsys flame view):
```
[  0.123s ] stream 3: cudaMemcpyAsync HtoD size=12KB (burst x48)
[  0.126s ] stream 1: cuLaunchKernel small_infer_kernel duration=0.45ms (queued)
[  0.128s ] stream 3: cudaMemcpyAsync HtoD size=12KB (burst x32)
[  0.130s ] OS: scheduling gap (prefetch-thread) 92ms
[  0.220s ] stream 1: cuLaunchKernel small_infer_kernel duration=0.48ms (executing)
```

tonny: perfect, this matches the hypothesis. keep the thread updates short — we'll review the PR today. :eyes:
